subject: English
topic: Direct and Indirect Speech — Reporting Across Tenses (W10)

questions.stem:
Convert to Indirect Speech:
"I am happy today," she said.

options.option_text: She said that she is happy today.
She said that she was happy that day.
She said that I am happy today.
She told that she was happy today.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Rules applied: (1) 'am' (Present) → 'was' (Past) in indirect speech. (2) 'I' → 'she' (pronoun change). (3) 'today' → 'that day' (time adverb change). (4) The reporting verb 'said' requires no 'to/that' + object; 'said that' is correct. Trap: A keeps 'is' and 'today' unchanged; C keeps the pronoun 'I'; D uses 'told' without an object (incorrect usage of 'told').

questions.stem:
Convert to Indirect Speech:
He said, "I will come tomorrow."

options.option_text: He said that he will come tomorrow.
He said that he would come the next day.
He said that he came the next day.
He told that he would come tomorrow.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Rules: (1) 'will' → 'would' (tense back-shift). (2) 'I' → 'he'. (3) 'tomorrow' → 'the next day' (time change). Trap: A keeps 'will' and 'tomorrow' unchanged (no back-shift); C changes to Simple Past 'came' (wrong — 'would come' is the modal past); D uses 'told' without an object ('told him' would be needed).

questions.stem:
Convert to Indirect Speech:
She said to me, "Do you like music?"

options.option_text: She told me if I like music.
She asked me if I liked music.
She asked me whether I like music.
She said me whether I liked music.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Rules for Yes/No questions: (1) Reporting verb changes to 'asked'. (2) 'Do you like' → 'if/whether I liked' (tense back-shift + subordinate clause structure). (3) Pronoun 'you' → 'I' (perspective of the person spoken to). Trap: A uses 'told' (wrong verb for questions); C keeps 'like' (no tense back-shift); D uses 'said me' (ungrammatical — 'said' doesn't take an indirect object without 'to').

questions.stem:
Convert to Indirect Speech:
The teacher said to the students, "Be quiet."

options.option_text: The teacher said to the students to be quiet.
The teacher told the students that be quiet.
The teacher told the students to be quiet.
The teacher asked the students that they be quiet.

questions.explanation: C is correct. For imperative sentences (commands): reporting verb → 'told/asked/ordered/requested' + object + to + infinitive. 'Be quiet' → 'to be quiet'. Trap: A uses 'said to' instead of 'told' (grammatically awkward for commands); B inserts 'that' which is only for declarative sentences; D uses 'asked' + 'that clause' (wrong structure for imperatives).

questions.stem:
Convert to Indirect Speech:
He said, "I have been working since morning."

options.option_text: He said that he has been working since morning.
He said that he had been working since that morning.
He said that he was working since that morning.
He said that he had worked since morning.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Present Perfect Continuous ('have been working') → Past Perfect Continuous ('had been working') in indirect speech. Time word 'since morning' → 'since that morning'. Trap: A keeps 'has been working' (no tense back-shift); C changes to Past Continuous 'was working' (loses the continuity/duration aspect); D uses Past Perfect Simple 'had worked' (drops the continuous aspect).

questions.stem:
Convert to Indirect Speech:
She said, "Honesty is the best policy."

options.option_text: She said that honesty was the best policy.
She said that honesty is the best policy.
She told that honesty is the best policy.
She said that honesty had been the best policy.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Universal truths, proverbs, and scientific facts do NOT undergo tense back-shift in indirect speech — they remain in Present tense. 'Honesty is the best policy' is a proverb (universal truth), so 'is' remains unchanged. Trap: A applies the usual back-shift to 'was' — incorrect for universal truths; D shifts to Past Perfect (entirely wrong); C uses 'told' without an indirect object.

questions.stem:
Convert to Indirect Speech:
"What a beautiful painting!" she exclaimed.

options.option_text: She exclaimed what a beautiful painting it was.
She exclaimed that it was a very beautiful painting.
She said that what a beautiful painting it was.
She told that it was a beautiful painting.

questions.explanation: B is correct. For exclamatory sentences: (1) Reporting verb remains 'exclaimed'. (2) 'What a/an + adjective + noun' → 'that it was a very + adjective + noun'. The exclamatory structure is converted to a declarative clause with 'very' emphasising the degree. Trap: A retains the exclamatory 'what' structure inside indirect speech (grammatically incorrect in standard indirect speech); C inserts 'that' before 'what' (double clause marker); D uses 'told' (wrong verb).

questions.stem:
Convert to Indirect Speech:
He said to her, "May you live long!"

options.option_text: He said to her that she may live long.
He told her that she might live long.
He wished her that she might live long.
He prayed that may she live long.

questions.explanation: C is correct. 'May + subject + verb' in a wish/blessing → 'wished + object + that + subject + might + verb'. 'May' → 'might' (back-shift of modal). The appropriate reporting verb for a blessing is 'wished'. Trap: A uses 'said to her' and 'may' (no back-shift); B uses 'told' (acceptable but 'wished' is preferred for blessings/wishes); D retains the inverted 'may she' structure inside indirect speech (grammatically incorrect).

questions.stem:
Convert to Indirect Speech:
She said, "If I had known, I would have helped you."

options.option_text: She said that if she had known, she would have helped me.
She said that if she knew, she would help me.
She said that if she had known, she would help me.
She said that if she would have known, she would have helped me.

questions.explanation: A is correct. This is a Third Conditional (past hypothetical) in direct speech. Past Perfect and 'would have + past participle' do NOT change further in indirect speech — they are already the most back-shifted forms. Only the pronoun changes: 'I' → 'she', 'you' → 'me'. Trap: B shifts to Second Conditional (incorrect, changes the hypothetical type); C keeps 'would help' instead of 'would have helped'; D introduces 'would have known' (non-standard and incorrect conditional form).

questions.stem:
Convert to Indirect Speech:
The teacher asked, "Who discovered America?"

options.option_text: The teacher asked who discovered America.
The teacher asked that who discovered America.
The teacher asked who had discovered America.
The teacher asked who has discovered America.

questions.explanation: C is correct. For Wh-questions in indirect speech: (1) Reporting verb → 'asked'. (2) 'who' remains as the connector (no 'if/whether'). (3) Word order becomes declarative: 'who discovered' → 'who had discovered' (tense back-shift: Simple Past → Past Perfect). (4) No question mark in indirect speech. Trap: A keeps Simple Past 'discovered' (no back-shift); B wrongly inserts 'that' after 'asked'; D uses Present Perfect 'has discovered' (wrong direction of tense shift).
